Solve the expression using the **BODMAS** rule by prioritising the **bracket** and **multiplication**.

73 + 88 − 64 + (62) × 2 − 99

161 − 64 + 124 − 99 = 122

**∴ The correct answer is 122.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 73 + 88 − 64 + (47 + 15) × 2 − 99

**Method Used:** **BODMAS Rule** (Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

⇒ 73 + 88 − 64 + (62) × 2 − 99

⇒ 73 + 88 − 64 + 124 − 99

⇒ (73 + 88 + 124) − (64 + 99)

⇒ 285 − 163

⇒ 122

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

VBODMAS Rule

The acronym **VBODMAS** helps remember the order: **Vinculum** (Bar), **Bracket**, **Of**, **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**.

Types of Brackets

Solve brackets in this specific order: **Bar/Vinculum** → **Small Brackets** ( ) → **Curly Brackets** { } → **Square Brackets** [ ].

Left to Right Rule

For operations of the same priority (like Addition/Subtraction or Multiplication/Division), always calculate from **left to right**.

questions.question: 63 + 41 - 29 + (33 of 1) - 18 + 26 ÷ 2 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply **BODMAS**: Solve **Of** (33 × 1 = 33) and **Division** (26 ÷ 2 = 13) first.

Expression becomes: 63 + 41 − 29 + 33 − 18 + 13.

Combine **positive terms**: 63 + 41 + 33 + 13 = 150.

Combine **negative terms**: 29 + 18 = 47.

Subtract: 150 − 47 = 103.

**∴ The correct answer is 103.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** 63 + 41 − 29 + (33 of 1) − 18 + 26 ÷ 2

Using the **BODMAS** rule (Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction):

⇒ 63 + 41 − 29 + (33 × 1) − 18 + 26 ÷ 2

⇒ 63 + 41 − 29 + 33 − 18 + 26 ÷ 2 (Solving **Of**)

⇒ 63 + 41 − 29 + 33 − 18 + 13 (Solving **Division**)

⇒ 104 − 29 + 33 − 18 + 13 (Solving **Addition** from left)

⇒ 75 + 33 − 18 + 13 (Solving **Subtraction**)

⇒ 108 − 18 + 13

⇒ 90 + 13

⇒ 103

**∴ The correct answer is 103.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It defines the order of operations: **Brackets** (), **Of** (multiplication priority), **Division** (÷), **Multiplication** (×), **Addition** (+), and **Subtraction** (−).

Priority of Of

The **Of** operator is essentially a multiplication but must be evaluated before **Division** and **Multiplication** according to the hierarchy.

Sign Management

Grouping all positive integers together and all negative integers together can simplify long chains of **Addition** and **Subtraction** to prevent errors.

questions.question: Which of the following lies between (1/4) & (3/4)?

Target Range: 1/4 = **0.25** and 3/4 = **0.75**.

**Given:**

Lower limit fraction = 1/4

Upper limit fraction = 3/4

**Formula Used:**

To check if fraction **x** lies between **a** and **b**, the condition is: **a 0.75) → **Invalid**

⇒ Checking Option 3: 9 ÷ 11 = **0.818...** (0.818 > 0.75) → **Invalid**

⇒ Checking Option 4: 15 ÷ 17 = **0.882...** (0.882 > 0.75) → **Invalid**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Comparing Fractions (Cross-Multiplication)

To compare a/b and c/d, check the products (a × d) and (b × c). If ad > bc, then a c/d.

Density Property of Rational Numbers

Between any two **rational numbers**, there are infinitely many other rational numbers. A simple way to find one is by taking the average: (a + b) ÷ 2.

Decimal Conversion Shortcut

Memorizing common fraction-to-decimal values (like 1/11 ≈ 0.09, 1/13 ≈ 0.077) helps in solving comparison questions within seconds.

questions.question: (9.8 + 1.8)² - 4 × 9.8 × 1.8 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The given expression follows the **Algebraic Identity**: (a + b)² − 4ab = (a − b)².

Here, let a = 9.8 and b = 1.8.

Applying the identity: (9.8 − 1.8)² = 8².

Result = 64.

**∴ The correct answer is 64.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (9.8 + 1.8)² − 4 × 9.8 × 1.8

**Method:** Direct Calculation using **BODMAS** and **Squares**.

⇒ Step 1: Solve the bracket (9.8 + 1.8) = 11.6

⇒ Step 2: Calculate the **Square** of 11.6 → 11.6 × 11.6 = 134.56

⇒ Step 3: Calculate the product 4 × 9.8 × 1.8

⇒ 4 × 17.64 = 70.56

⇒ Step 4: **Subtract** the values: 134.56 − 70.56 = 64

**∴ The correct answer is 64.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Algebraic Identities

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b².

Relationship between Identities

(a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab, which can be rearranged as (a + b)² − 4ab = (a − b)².

Difference of Squares

a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b). This is useful for **simplification** of large products.

questions.question: The area of a rhombus is 336 square cm. One of the diagonal is 14 cm. What is the perimeter (in cm) of the rhombus?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Area formula**: Area = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂ ⇒ 336 = (1/2) × 14 × d₂ ⇒ d₂ = 48 cm.

Apply **Pythagorean triplet** (7, 24, 25) for the right triangle formed by half-diagonals: Side (a) = 25 cm.

**Perimeter** = 4 × side = 4 × 25 = 100 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 100 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Area** of rhombus = 336 cm² and **diagonal** d₁ = 14 cm.

**Formula Used:**

1) Area = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂

2) Side (a) = √[(d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)²]

3) Perimeter = 4 × a

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0aa6b33389ef7ce441d183dc5038c431df5068e3d17b2c294d4a5105044b321b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 336 = (1/2) × 14 × d₂

⇒ 336 = 7 × d₂

⇒ d₂ = 336 ÷ 7 = 48 cm

⇒ Half of diagonals: d₁/2 = 7 cm and d₂/2 = 24 cm

⇒ **Side (a)** = √[7² + 24²]

⇒ a = √[49 + 576] = √625 = 25 cm

⇒ **Perimeter** = 4 × 25 = 100 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 100 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Rhombus

All four sides are equal, and the **diagonals bisect each other** at right angles (90°).

Relation between Sides and Diagonals

The side 'a' and diagonals 'd₁' and 'd₂' follow the relation: 4a² = d₁² + d₂².

Common Pythagorean Triplets

Triplets like (7, 24, 25), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17) are frequently used in geometry problems involving **right-angled triangles**.

questions.question: The adjacent angles of a parallelogram are in the ratio of 4 : 5. What are the measure (in degrees) of the larger angle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **parallelogram**, the sum of **adjacent angles** is always 180°.

Given **ratio** = 4 : 5

Total units = 4 + 5 = 9 units

9 units = 180° ⇒ 1 unit = 20°

**Larger angle** = 5 units = 5 × 20° = 100°

**∴ The correct answer is 100°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of **adjacent angles** = 4 : 5

**Formula Used:**

The **adjacent angles** of a **parallelogram** are **supplementary** (sum = 180°).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e49313d8ae15d7f6d2ce4c69024ef5c052ba454a3bbc348840e3c1ee3fd760d5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the measures of the **adjacent angles** be 4x and 5x.

⇒ 4x + 5x = 180°

⇒ 9x = 180°

⇒ x = 180° ÷ 9

⇒ x = 20°

⇒ Larger angle = 5x = 5 × 20° = 100°

⇒ Smaller angle = 4x = 4 × 20° = 80°

**∴ The correct answer is 100°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Parallelogram

Opposite angles are always equal, and the sum of all interior angles is 360°.

Consecutive Interior Angles

When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, consecutive interior angles (like adjacent angles in a parallelogram) are supplementary.

Diagonals of a Parallelogram

The diagonals bisect each other but are not necessarily equal in length unless the figure is a rectangle.

questions.question: Least Common Multiple of 11 and 30 is X, Highest Common Factor of 11 and 30 is Y. Then what is the value of (X - 2Y)?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Numbers **11** and **30** are **co-prime** (no common factors except 1). For co-prime numbers, **HCF (Y) = 1** and **LCM (X) = Product** of the numbers. **X** = 11 × 30 = **330** and **Y = 1**. Value = **X − 2Y** = 330 − 2(1) = **328**. **∴ The correct answer is 328.**

questions.question: The Highest Common Factor of two numbers is 7 and their Least Common Multiple is 252. The ratio of the numbers is 9 : 4. What is the sum of the two numbers?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ The **Ratio** of the two numbers is 9 : 4 and their **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** is 7. Total ratio units = 9 + 4 = 13 units. Since the **HCF** represents the value of 1 ratio unit, then 1 unit = 7. **Sum of the numbers** = 13 units × 7 = 91. **∴ The correct answer is 91.**

questions.question: Which number is 60 percent less than 50 percent of 600?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Required Value** = (100 − 60)% of (50% of 600)

⇒ 40% × (50% × 600)

⇒ 0.4 × 300 = 120

**∴ The correct answer is 120.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Base Number = 600

First Step: Find 50% of the number.

Second Step: Find the number which is 60% less than the result of the first step.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fc48e9e5b2e7ccfdd447c26f1d4731148213c89474ed2c7df3fde64fe1d8d81c.png] 

**Step 1: Calculate 50% of 600**

⇒ Value₁ = (50 ÷ 100) × 600

⇒ Value₁ = 0.5 × 600 = 300

**Step 2: Calculate 60% less than Value₁**

⇒ Final Value = Value₁ − (60% of Value₁)

⇒ Final Value = 300 − (0.6 × 300)

⇒ Final Value = 300 − 180

⇒ Final Value = 120

**∴ The correct answer is 120.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Decrease Formula

To find a value x% less than A, use the formula: Result = A × (100 − x) ÷ 100.

Successive Percentages

When multiple percentage changes are applied, the final multiplier is the product of individual multipliers (e.g., 0.5 × 0.4 = 0.2 of original).

Fraction Equivalents

Memorizing common fractions like 50% = 1/2 and 60% = 3/5 helps in faster mental calculation.

questions.question: 50 percent of 450 eggs are rotten. How many eggs are NOT rotten?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since **50%** of the eggs are rotten, the remaining **50%** are **NOT rotten**.

In mathematics, **50%** is equivalent to **half** of the total value.

Number of eggs NOT rotten = 450 ÷ 2 = 225.

**∴ The correct answer is 225 eggs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of eggs = 450

Percentage of **rotten eggs** = 50%

**Formula Used:**

Number of items = (Percentage ÷ 100) × Total Quantity

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7486cf6ee6cb4c99bd21fdd5a3399857d5e7577e86f8583d88e6897a9b4a16fa.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total eggs = 450

⇒ Number of rotten eggs = 50% of 450

⇒ Rotten eggs = (50 ÷ 100) × 450 = 225

⇒ Number of eggs NOT rotten = Total eggs − Rotten eggs

⇒ Number of eggs NOT rotten = 450 − 225 = 225

**∴ The correct answer is 225 eggs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Basics

Percentage means **per hundred**. To find x% of a value y, the calculation is (x × y) ÷ 100.

Fraction Equivalents

Converting common percentages to fractions can speed up calculations: **50% = 1/2**, 25% = 1/4, 75% = 3/4, and 20% = 1/5.

Complementary Percentage

If a certain category is **A%** of a total, the remaining category is always **(100 − A)%** of that same total.

questions.question: A person sells an article at the profit of 40 percent. Cost price and selling price both are decreased by 50 percent. What will be the new profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If both the **Cost Price** and the **Selling Price** are multiplied by the same scaling factor, the **Profit Percentage** remains constant.

Decreasing both prices by **50 percent** is equivalent to multiplying them by a factor of 0.5.

Since both are scaled equally, the ratio of **Selling Price** to **Cost Price** does not change.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png]

questions.question: A person sells an article at the loss of 30 percent. Cost price and selling price both are decreased by 40 percent. What will be the new loss percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If both the **Cost Price (CP)** and **Selling Price (SP)** of an article are increased or decreased by the **same percentage**, the **Profit or Loss percentage** remains **constant**.

This occurs because the **ratio** between the Selling Price and Cost Price (SP/CP) does not change when both terms are multiplied by the same factor.

Initial loss = 30% ⇒ Final loss = 30%.

**∴ The correct answer is 30%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial loss = 30%, decrease in both CP and SP = 40%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6c19378d1eff79ca8314571c16814f0ecc4e2b9f5751fb0a74a81e7b17791a31.png] 

⇒ Let **Initial CP** = 100

⇒ **Initial SP** = 100 − 30% of 100 = 70

⇒ **New CP** = 100 − (40% of 100) = 100 − 40 = 60

⇒ **New SP** = 70 − (40% of 70) = 70 − 28 = 42

⇒ **New Loss** = New CP − New SP = 60 − 42 = 18

⇒ **New Loss %** = (New Loss ÷ New CP) × 100

⇒ **New Loss %** = (18 ÷ 60) × 100 = 3 ÷ 10 × 100 = 30%

**∴ The correct answer is 30%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Invariant Percentage Rule

When every component of a ratio (like SP and CP) is multiplied or divided by a **constant non-zero value**, the percentage relationship between them remains **unchanged**.

Loss Percentage Calculation

Loss % = [(CP − SP) ÷ CP] × 100. Always ensure the **Cost Price** is the denominator unless the problem specifies calculation on the selling price.

Selling Price for Loss

SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100. This formula helps calculate the price needed to maintain a specific **loss threshold**.

questions.question: R did 2/3 part of a work on first day. He did 1/4 part of the remaining work on second day. If the total work is 84 units, then how much work (in units) is remaining now?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Successive Remainder** method to find the final remaining part.

Remaining fraction after Day 1 = 1 − 2/3 = 1/3

Remaining fraction after Day 2 = 1/3 × (1 − 1/4) = 1/3 × 3/4 = 1/4

**Remaining work** = Total work × 1/4 = 84 × 1/4 = 21 units.

**∴ The correct answer is 21 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Total work** = 84 units, Day 1 work = 2/3 of total, Day 2 work = 1/4 of remaining.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f5c44ab1ec2a619588328b37d4c5ea97e9ea62ab4e8c9b3b201b3fbfdf12684b.png] 

⇒ Work done on **Day 1** = 2/3 × 84 = 56 units

⇒ **Remaining work** after Day 1 = 84 − 56 = 28 units

⇒ Work done on **Day 2** = 1/4 × 28 = 7 units

⇒ **Final remaining work** = 28 − 7 = 21 units

**∴ The correct answer is 21 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work-Fraction Relation

Total Work is always considered as 1 unit or 100%. If a fraction 'x' is done, then (1 − x) is the remaining work.

Successive Remainder Formula

If fractions a, b, c... are taken from the **remaining** amount successively, the final remainder is Total × (1−a) × (1−b) × (1−c)...

Work and Efficiency

Total Work = Efficiency × Time. In fractional problems, the denominator usually represents the 'Total units' relative to that specific step.

questions.question: A and B are employed in a work. A worked for 5 days and B worked for 6 days. Per day work of A and B is 3 units and 2 units respectively. Difference between the shares of A and B is Rs. 600. What is the share (in Rs.) of A?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of work done by **A** and **B** = (Time × Efficiency)A : (Time × Efficiency)B

Work Ratio = (**5 days** × **3 units**) : (**6 days** × **2 units**) = 15 : 12 = **5 : 4**

Difference in ratio parts = 5 − 4 = 1 part

Given, 1 part = **₹600**

Share of **A** = 5 parts = 5 × 600 = **₹3000**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A worked for **5 days** with **3 units/day** efficiency; B worked for **6 days** with **2 units/day** efficiency. Difference in their shares = **₹600**.

**Formula:** Total Work = Time × Efficiency | Share ∝ Total Work Done

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Efficiency**
 **Total Work Done**
 
 

 **A**
 5
 3
 15 units
 
 

 **B**
 6
 2
 12 units
 
 

⇒ Work done by **A** = 5 × 3 = **15 units**

⇒ Work done by **B** = 6 × 2 = **12 units**

⇒ Difference in work = 15 − 12 = **3 units**

⇒ According to the question, 3 units = **₹600**

⇒ 1 unit = 600 ÷ 3 = **₹200**

⇒ Share of **A** = 15 units × 200 = **₹3000**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Wages Rule

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the **actual work performed**. If the time worked is different for each person, use the formula: Wages Ratio = (E₁ × T₁) : (E₂ × T₂).

Efficiency and Wage Relationship

If all persons work for the **same duration** of time, their wages are distributed directly in the ratio of their **individual efficiencies**.

Total Wage Calculation

Total Wage = Wage per unit work × Total work units. Alternatively, Total Wage = Sum of individual shares.

questions.question: Speed of stream is 5 km/hr. Speed of the boat in still water is 17 km/hr. What is the downstream speed (in km/hr) of the boat?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a boat moving with the flow, **Downstream Speed** = Speed in **Still Water** + Speed of **Stream**.

Downstream Speed = 17 + 5 = 22 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 22 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the boat in **still water** (u) = 17 km/hr

Speed of the **stream** (v) = 5 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Downstream speed (Dₛ) = u + v

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3d847d75bc0bd7c6737b7fefb23b5dcf3dc6a2632e473a0f22e73f75bd14d1a0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Downstream speed = 17 + 5

⇒ Downstream speed = 22 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 22 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Upstream Speed

When the boat moves against the flow of the stream: Upstream Speed = Speed in still water − Speed of stream.

Speed of Boat in Still Water

It can be calculated if downstream (D) and upstream (U) speeds are known: Speed in still water = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Speed of Stream

It can be calculated as: Speed of stream = (D − U) ÷ 2.

questions.question: A car covers a distance of 36 km in 60 minutes. If its speed is decreased by 20 km/hr, then what will be the time (in minutes) taken by it to cover the same distance?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ **Initial speed** = 36 km ÷ 1 hr = **36 km/hr**. **Reduced speed** = 36 − 20 = **16 km/hr**. Speed ratio = 36 : 16 = 9 : 4. Since **distance** is constant, Time ratio = 4 : 9. 4 units = **60 min** ⇒ 9 units = (60 ÷ 4) × 9 = 15 × 9 = **135 min**. **∴ The correct answer is 135 min.**

questions.question: The ratio of two number A and B is 5 : 3. If both numbers are increased by 5, then the ratio of A and B becomes 3 : 2. What is the sum of initial values of A and B?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Initial **Ratio A : B** = 5 : 3 (Difference = 2 units) Final **Ratio A : B** = 3 : 2 = 6 : 4 (Multiplied by 2 to make difference = 2 units) Increase in each part = 6 − 5 = 1 unit → 5 Sum of initial values = 5 + 3 = 8 units Total **Sum** = 8 × 5 = 40 **∴ The correct answer is 40.**

questions.question: An article is sold for 40 percent profit. The value of discount given is equal to (5/14) of the marked price. Cost price of the article is how much percent less than its marked price?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Let **Marked Price** (MP) = 14 units ⇒ **Discount** = 5 units. **Selling Price** (SP) = 14 − 5 = 9 units. Given **Profit** = 40% ⇒ CP = SP ÷ 1.4 = 9 ÷ 1.4 = 45/7 units. Difference = 14 − 45/7 = 53/7 units. **Percentage** less = (53/7 ÷ 14) × 100 = 5300 ÷ 98 ≈ 54.08%. **∴ The correct answer is 54.08%.**

questions.question: The marked price of an article is 50 percent more than its cost price. If the profit earned is 25 percent, then what is the discount offered on the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio **CP : MP** = 100 : 150 = 2 : 3.

Ratio **CP : SP** = 100 : 125 = 4 : 5 (since **Profit** is 25%).

Equating **CP** in both ratios: **CP : SP : MP** = 4 : 5 : 6.

**Discount** = **MP** − **SP** = 6 − 5 = 1 unit.

**Discount %** = (1 ÷ 6) × 100 = 16.67%.

**∴ The correct answer is 16.67 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Markup Percentage** = 50%

**Profit Percentage** = 25%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6dc26fb84ab1848b1747f39efe5006fdcbbfd3751d25648132eaf9124ae41b0f.png] 

**Formula Used:**

**Selling Price (SP)** = **Cost Price (CP)** + **Profit**

**Discount** = **Marked Price (MP)** − **Selling Price (SP)**

**Discount %** = (**Discount** ÷ **Marked Price**) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of the article be 100.

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 50% of 100 = 150.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 100 + 25% of 100 = 125.

⇒ **Discount Amount** = 150 − 125 = 25.

⇒ **Discount Percentage** = (25 ÷ 150) × 100.

⇒ **Discount Percentage** = (1 ÷ 6) × 100 = 16.666...%

⇒ **Discount Percentage** ≈ 16.67%.

**∴ The correct answer is 16.67 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Markup and Profit Relation

The relationship between **Marked Price (MP)** and **Cost Price (CP)** can be expressed as: **MP / CP** = (100 + **Profit %**) / (100 − **Discount %**).

Effective Discount Formula

For two **successive discounts** of a% and b%, the single **equivalent discount** is given by: (a + b − ab/100)%.

Profit and Discount Calculation

**Profit** is always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)**, whereas the **Discount** is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**.

questions.question: What is the fourth proportion of 18, 4 and 45?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Fourth Proportional (d)** of three numbers **a**, **b**, and **c** is given by the formula:

**d = (b × c) ÷ a**

Here, **a = 18**, **b = 4**, and **c = 45**.

⇒ **Fourth Proportional = (4 × 45) ÷ 18 = 180 ÷ 18 = 10**

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The three numbers are **18**, **4**, and **45**.

**Formula Used:** If four numbers **a**, **b**, **c**, and **d** are in **proportion**, then **a : b :: c : d**, which implies **a ÷ b = c ÷ d** or **a × d = b × c**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3a02230afc780e3e9e51605aac50b3f8b7974230c8fb92f1ee75c4b98d78d4b6.png] 

Let the **fourth proportion** be **x**.

⇒ **18 : 4 :: 45 : x**

⇒ **18 ÷ 4 = 45 ÷ x**

⇒ **18 × x = 45 × 4**

⇒ **18x = 180**

⇒ **x = 180 ÷ 18**

⇒ **x = 10**

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The **mean proportional** between two numbers **a** and **b** is calculated as **√(a × b)**.

Third Proportional

If **a**, **b**, and **c** are in **continued proportion** (**a : b = b : c**), then **c** is the **third proportional**, given by **c = b² ÷ a**.

Invertendo and Alternendo

If **a : b = c : d**, then **b : a = d : c** (**Invertendo**) and **a : c = b : d** (**Alternendo**).
